title: Fake bank SMS: account blocked, confirm your OTP
text: A message claiming to be from MCB, SBM or another bank says your account or card is blocked or suspended and asks you to click a link, log in, or share the one-time password (OTP) sent to your phone. Banks never ask for your OTP, PIN or full card number by SMS, call or WhatsApp. Do not click the link. Call your bank on the number printed on the back of your card.
source: Unverified team summary of common bank phishing patterns; check against bank websites before the demo

title: Fake Mauritius Post parcel held, pay a small customs fee
text: An SMS or email says a parcel is held at customs or could not be delivered and asks you to pay a small fee (for example Rs 75) through a link. The link leads to a fake payment page that steals card details. Do not pay through links in messages. Check delivery only on the postal service website you type in yourself.
source: Unverified team summary of parcel-fee phishing patterns; check before the demo

title: Fake CEB or CWA disconnection threat
text: A message says your electricity (CEB) or water (CWA) will be cut today unless you pay an overdue bill immediately through a link, a mobile money transfer or by calling a number. Real utility notices do not demand instant payment by link. Check your bill with the utility using the number on a paper bill.
source: Unverified team summary; check before the demo

title: Fake Emtel or my.t promotion or prize
text: A message says you won a prize, free data or a phone in an Emtel or my.t (Mauritius Telecom) promotion and asks you to click a link, pay a delivery or processing fee, or share personal details to claim it. You cannot win a contest you did not enter, and real prizes never require a fee.
source: Unverified team summary; check before the demo

title: Fake MRA tax refund email
text: An email claiming to be from the Mauritius Revenue Authority (MRA) says you are owed a tax refund and asks you to click a link and enter bank or card details to receive it. Tax refunds are not claimed through email links. Log in only on the MRA website you type in yourself.
source: Unverified team summary; check before the demo

title: Fake police call: your son or grandson is arrested
text: A caller pretends to be a police officer or lawyer and says a family member was arrested or had an accident and needs money now for bail, a fine or hospital fees. They insist it is urgent and secret. Hang up. Call the family member directly on their usual number, or call the police yourself.
source: Unverified team summary of impersonation-call patterns; check before the demo

title: WhatsApp 'Hi Mum, this is my new number'
text: A WhatsApp message from an unknown number says 'Hi Mum' or 'Hi Dad, I lost my phone, this is my new number' and soon asks for money for an urgent bill. Call your child on their old number or ask a question only they would know before sending anything.
source: Unverified team summary; check before the demo

title: Investment or crypto group promising big returns
text: You are added to a WhatsApp or Telegram group, or contacted on social media, promising guaranteed high returns from crypto, forex or trading. Early small payouts build trust, then withdrawals are blocked unless you pay more fees. Guaranteed returns are a scam sign. Check with the Financial Services Commission before investing.
source: Unverified team summary; check before the demo

title: Job offer that asks for an upfront fee
text: A job offer, often work-from-home, liking videos or a job abroad, asks you to pay for registration, training, a visa or a uniform before you start, or asks you to receive and forward money. Real employers do not charge you to get hired.
source: Unverified team summary; check before the demo

title: Romance scam: online partner asks for money
text: Someone you met online, often claiming to work abroad, the military or on an oil rig, builds a relationship quickly then asks for money for travel, customs, medical bills or an emergency. Never send money to someone you have not met in person.
source: Unverified team summary; check before the demo

title: How to report: CERT-MU and MAUCORS
text: Online scams and phishing can be reported to CERT-MU through the MAUCORS online reporting platform. Keep screenshots of the message, the sender number and any link before reporting.
source: Unverified team note; confirm the reporting URL before the demo

title: How to report: Police Cybercrime Unit
text: If you lost money or were threatened, report it to the Police, which has a Cybercrime Unit, at your nearest police station. Bring the messages and payment details.
source: Unverified team note; confirm contact details before the demo

title: If you shared card or OTP details, call your bank now
text: If you clicked a link, entered card details or shared an OTP, call your bank immediately on the number printed on the back of your card to block the card. Never use a phone number given in the suspicious message.
